body.heading: The invisible shift
paragraphs: The train ran because someone inspected brakes at 4 a.m. The ward was clean because someone worked the night shift with a mop and no audience. The library book was reshelved, the road gritted, the software patched. A smooth day is a crowd scene in which almost everyone is uncredited.
Noticing this does not oblige you to anything exhausting. It simply corrects the story that your life runs on your own efforts.

body.heading: Thanks that travels
paragraphs: You can thank the unseen more often than you think: the note left for the cleaning staff, the kind word to the depot worker, the review that names the team, the complaint-free patience when a tired system slows down. Thanks addressed to a role still lands on a person.
And where you hold any small power — a team, a rota, a budget — thanks can become structural: credit given in the meeting, names included in the report, the night shift remembered at bonus time.

body.heading: A practice of peripheral vision
paragraphs: Try one deliberate act of peripheral gratitude a week: spot one invisible contribution and acknowledge it somehow. The practice changes the practitioner most. The world starts to look less like a service and more like a collaboration.
Which, on inspection, is exactly what it always was.

takeaway: Notice one invisible contribution a week, and let thanks travel to the people you will never meet.
